{{Quote|I am aboard an ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer. Built at the Kuat Drive Shipyards. It possesses many useful systems and capabilities.|The [[Scourge]]|<ref name="DD 1" />}}
The '''''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer''' was a model of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] in the service of the [[Imperial Navy]]. A wedge-shaped [[capital ship]], it bristled with weapons emplacements, assault [[troop]]s, boarding craft, and [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]] starfighters. In the [[Imperial Era|era]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], its [[Bridge (starship)|command bridge]] was staffed by the finest crewmen in the [[navy]].

At first, [[Star Destroyer]]s were deployed to [[sector]]s and [[Star system|systems]] caught in the aftermath of the [[Clone Wars]], where they would crush any signs of sedition. During the [[Galactic Civil War]] the Destroyer's role changed to hunting down high value [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel]] targets and bases. They fought in notable battles such as the [[Battle of Hoth]] and the [[Battle of Endor]]. The [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] was a derivative of the ''Imperial I''-class.

==Characteristics==
===Dimensions===
[[File:ISD_blueprints.png|thumb|left|175px|Technical forward, aft and lateral schematics of an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]]
The ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer was the first model of the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class]] line<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> of [[Star Destroyer]]s<ref name="Battles">''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]''</ref> designed by [[Lira Wessex]]<ref name="SW BMF 20" /> and used by the [[Galactic Empire]]'s [[Imperial Navy]].<ref name="USW NE" /> Despite the Star Destroyer being considered a [[capital ship]] under Imperial doctrine, the [[Anaxes War College System]] classified it as a [[destroyer]].<ref name="Battles" />

With a length of 1,600 [[meter]]s and a width of 985 meters,<ref name="SW DORVG" />, the wedge-shaped ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer<ref name="USW NE" /> was 445 meters longer<ref name="dbRAC">{{Databank|republic-attack-cruiser|Republic Attack Cruiser}}</ref> than its immediate predecessor, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]], which had been developed for the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars]].<ref name="DB ISD">{{Databank|imperial-star-destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer}}</ref> In keeping with the Empire's habit of favoring muted colors whenever possible,<ref name="newhero">''[[Star Wars Rebels: A New Hero]]''</ref> the hull of the Imperial-class was painted in whitish gray,<ref name="USW NE" /> a stark change from the ''Venator''-class of the Clone Wars era which featured red markings<ref name="dbRAC" />

===Crew requirements & quarters===
''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers had over 37,000 crew on board— 9,235 officers and 27,850 enlisted personnel. The complement of 9,700 [[stormtrooper]]s added to a total of 46,785 crew and passengers,<ref name="USW NE" /> with 2,000 of those being the bare minimum
required to safely operate the ship.<ref name="SW22" /> Like other Star Destroyer classes, a single [[Internal Affairs]] officer was stationed aboard the ship to scan the crew for signs of disloyalty and sedition, as well as interrogate any captured prisoners.<ref name="Lost Stars">''[[Lost Stars]]''</ref> As most ships in the Navy, Rebaxan Columni [[MSE-6 series repair droid]]s were employed to serve as messenger, repair and custodial assistants.<ref name="TFA Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

The officer's quarters were located right below the bridge, in the ship's [[Conning tower|command tower]].<ref name="Rey's Survival Guide">''[[Rey's Survival Guide]]''</ref> The officer barracks, gunnery crew quarters,<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> recreation areas,<ref name="SW DORVG" /> meeting rooms and [[prison|cell blocks]] were located on the second level<ref name="USW NE" /> of the ship's multi-tiered habitable superstructure,<ref name="SW DORVG" /> with four gradually upsloping shorter 'levels' eventually leading to the ships 'neck' which connected it to its upper command tower.<ref name="USW NE" /> On the contrary, the barracks for the 27,000 enlisted personnel were located on the ship's midsection, outside of the main superstructure.<ref name="SW DORVG" /> The ship was also equipped with specialized training rooms that could simulate various environmental conditions, including underwater combat,<ref name="DV 2017 13">[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]]</ref> [[simulator pod]]s for [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot]]s<ref name="TIE Onwer">''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]''</ref> as well as several [[Medcenter|medical substations]].<ref name="SW DORVG" />

To complement its impressive crew size, every ''Imperial''-class vessel carried consumables for 2 [[Standard year|years]],<ref name="AbEverything" /> with its liquid stores and holds for raw materials being located near its bow.<ref name="Rey's Survival Guide" /> On the "side" of the ship, in front of the [[hangar]]s, existed the lateral umbilical restocking vestibules.<ref name="SW ROUVG" />

===Armament and shielding===
{{Quote|This is an Imperial Star Destroyer. All vital equipment is shielded. Even twenty bombs will do nothing.|Prelate [[Verge]]|<ref name="Twilight Company">''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]''</ref>}}
[[File:GhostDestroysTractorBeam-Rebels-Legacy.png|thumb|left|220px|The ''[[Ghost]]'' flies away from the ''Relentless''{{'s}} destroyed ventral tractor beam projectors.]]
The ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer bristled with weapons emplacements. The most common weapons equipped onto Imperial I-class Star Destroyers were the 60 [[Taim & Bak]] [[XX-9 heavy turbolaser battery|XX-9 heavy turbolaser batteries]],<ref name="SWE NWAE" /> hooked into large arrays of auxiliary [[power cell]]s,<ref name="Rey's Survival Guide" /> 60 [[Borstel Galactic Defense|Borstel]] [[NK-7 ion cannon]]s, and ten [[Phylon Transport|Phylon]] [[Q7 tractor beam projector]]s dotted its whitish gray hull.<ref name="USW NE" /> The forward pursuit [[tractor beam]] array was located in the ship's very front,<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> while four other tractor beam projectors were located around the hanagr bay opening.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The ship also featured six dual heavy turbolaser turrets, two quad heavy turbolasers, three triple medium turbolasers, and two medium turbolasers. At both "ends" of the Star Destroyer existed an aft [[point-defense laser cannon]].<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> The Star Destroyer was equipped with [[LeGrange]] [[targeting computer]]s<ref name="SWE SOTEATR">{{EncyclopediaCite|Starships of the Empire and the Rebellion}}</ref> and a separate [[tractor beam targeting array]]<ref name="Droids in Destress book">[[Droids in Distress (book)|''Droids in Distress'' chapter book]]</ref> located at the top of the command tower.<ref name="SWCT" />

The heaviest and largest armament on the ship were the combined six dual heavy turbolaser turrets and two dual heavy [[ion cannon]] turrets<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> that were situated at each side of the dorsal superstructure flanking the command tower. With a diameter of 50 meters, each turbolaser was capable of ripping through heavy armor and overloading shields. Although it was difficult to hit small, fast-moving craft, even a glancing blow from those turrets would destroy them.<ref name="SW CVNE" /> Despite this impressive collection of weapons, the ''Imperial I''-class still had a large blindspot in its aft quarter, where none of them could reach. Enemy starfighters often exploited this weakness to deliver devastating attacks, although veteran captains aware of it would maneuver the ship to keep them away and deploy starfighter squadrons to repel most attacks.<ref name="Starships and Speeders" />

The ''Imperial I''-class was heavily shielded,<ref name="Starships and Speeders" /> and its armored durasteel plating<ref name="SW SDBookModel" /> durable enough to easily withstand a direct collision with a [[GR-75 medium transport]] with no damage to the hull.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Situated at the ventral side of the bow of the ISD was the navigational deflector generator,<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> accompanied by the hull deflector shield generator nearer towards vessel's rear.<ref name="SW DORVG" /> Two [[ISD-72x shield generator dome]]s were present upon the top of the command tower, at each side of the tractor beam targeting array,<ref name="SW BMF 20" /> to protect the tower, encompassing the bridge.<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> They also served as sensor arrays, which could scan up to six hundred thousand kilometers.<ref name="Thrawn: Treason">''[[Thrawn: Treason]]''</ref> Furthermore deflector shield projector ports were scattered around the habitable superstructure.<ref name="SW DORVG" />

===Complement and hangars===
[[File:DualTurbolaser.png|alt=|left|thumb|The foremost starboard dual heavy [[turbolaser]] turret on the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer, ''Intimidator'']]
The ''Imperial I''-class featured two vast hangar bays in its underside, on an opening large enough to hold an entire [[CR90 corvette]].<ref name="ANH" /> The roof of the opening was equipped with an [[electromagnet]]ic paralyzing pincer crane, which grabbed onto and disabled captured ships for boarding. One of the hangars, known as the primary attack hangar<ref name="SW CVNE" /> was used to host [[transport]]s and visiting [[shuttle]]s<ref name="Imperial Eyes">{{Rebels|Through Imperial Eyes}}</ref> as well as launch landing craft for planetary assaults,<ref name="DV 2017 13" /> while the other held the Star Destroyer's starfighter complement,<ref name="SW CVNE" /> consisting of seventy-two [[TIE series|TIE fighter series]] starfighters.<ref name="SW TIEBookModel" /> Another smaller bay on the opposite side of the attack hangar was used to receive returning TIEs,<ref name="SW CVNE" /> which were then transported in receiver-carriers to a debarkation station where TIE pilots exited their craft, and then moved to be stored in several launch bays surrounding the hangar opening. [[TIE/sa tactical bomber]]s were held in specialized armored compartments to protect the rest of the ship if their bombs detonated. Service and refueling bays surrounded the TIE stations to prepare their fighters for their next sorties before the craft were moved through transfer tunnels back to the launch hangar.<ref name="TIE Onwer" /> The ''Imperial I''-class was also equipped with another backup hangar at the front of the ship which was used to launch and receive shuttle craft for high-ranking officials.<ref name="SW CVNE" />

Besides its TIE squadrons, the ship also carried eight [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttles]], twenty [[All Terrain Armored Transport|AT-AT]] [[walker]]s, thirty [[All Terrain Scout Transport|AT-ST]] or [[All Terrain Defense Pod|AT-DP]] walkers, and fifteen [[K79-S80 Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial Troop Transports]].<ref name="USW NE" /> They could also carry several [[aerial landing platform]]s for use during planetary invasions.<ref name="DV 2017 13" />

Despite its fighter complement, ''Imperial I''-class vessels proved less effective against skilled rebel pilots than their ''Venator''-class predecessors had been against droid starfighters.<ref name="USW NE" /> They were nonetheless essential in the Imperial doctrine of planetary containment and fast infantry deployment, and the vessel was noted as one of the most resource-intensive ships in the Imperial Navy.<ref name="Twilight Company" />

''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers were equipped with several [[escape pod]]s equipped with emergency beacons, to allow the crew to abandon the ship in an emergency.<ref name="ZH" /> They also carried the necessary equipment to launch and retrieve [[Hyperdrive pod|hyperspace pods]], at least twelve of which were docked in a bay above the hangar opening.<ref name="Warhead" />

===Power and propulsion systems===
[[File:Devastator_Engines.png|thumb|left|200px|The active primary and secondary ion sublight engines of the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer, ''Devastator'']]
Powering the Destroyer were seven main engine units,<ref name="Droids in Destress book" /> including three [[Kuat Drive Yards]] [[Destroyer-I ion engine]]s and four [[Cygnus Spaceworks]] [[Gemon-4 ion engine]]s,<ref name="USW NE" /> which could accelerate the ship to speeds of up to 975 kph.<ref name="AbEverything" /> The ship however was not suited towards planetary atmospheres, in which full power was required to stay aloft. Any interruption in the power supply in atmosphere could be catastrophic to the vessel, despite all vital equipment being shielded.<ref name="Twilight Company" /> The primary power source on board the ship was a [[solar ionization reactor]] large enough relative to the rest of the craft to protrude with a ventral bulb,<ref name="Droids in Destress book" /> powering a massive cylindrical [[power generator]] surrounded by antiresonance plates<ref name="SW CVNE" /> located in sector 19-A on the ship's rear.<ref name="SW22" />

Although well-armored, a direct hit from [[proton torpedo]]es in that area would cause a breach in the generator venting tunnel, causing the reactor to overload and explode within seven [[Standard minute|minutes]]. To prevent ship-wide catastrophe it was possible to jettison the entire reactor assembly.<ref name="SW22" /> To allow the ship to continue to run in this event, the ''Imperial I''-class also carried a backup secondary reactor<ref name="SW23" /> to power the engines, and a subsidiary reactor<ref name="SW CVNE" /> to provide auxiliary power to the rest of the ship.<ref name="SW22" /> A third auxiliary reactor was located on the ship's prow.<ref name="SW CVNE" />

Engines were controlled in a massive room filled with walkways and [["Tulip" style Imperial work station]]s.<ref name="FATG">{{Rebels|Fire Across the Galaxy}}</ref> In order to jump to light-speed and enter [[hyperspace]] the ''Imperial''-class was equipped with a Class 2 [[hyperdrive]], while it was standard protocol to dump the ship's garbage before entering hyperspace in order to reduce the weight of the vessel.<ref name="USW NE" />

===Bridge===
[[File:Devastator_Bridge.png|thumb|left|250px|The bridge of the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer ''Devastator'']]
A prominent feature of the ''Imperial''-class was its [[Conning tower|bridge tower]].<ref name="Droids in Destress book" /> The command bridge itself featured two elongated pits set below floor level, whose walls were lined with monitors and control panels. In addition, six more duty station consoles were mounted freely in each pit aligned perpendicular to the walkway. High-ranking officers stood on a walkway surrounding the pits at the normal deck height,<ref name="Spark">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''</ref> an arrangement considered beneficial for denoting rank hierarchy within the ship.<ref name="TFA Visual Dictionary" /> The consoles mounted under the [[viewport]]s in this level carried a [[holoprojector]] used for officer communications<ref name="DV 2017 14">[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]]</ref> and the controls which allowed the [[Helm officer|helmsman]] to pilot the ship.<ref name="SW24">[[Star Wars (2015) 24|''Star Wars'' (2015) 24]]</ref>

A small room behind the main bridge existed separated by a single blast door, which had access to advanced communications equipment and a holographic imaging table.<ref name="Spark">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:Imperial_fleet_above_Lothal-Sw_Rebels_S3-Iron_Squadron.png|thumb|220px|[[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn's]] [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|Seventh Fleet]]]]
The ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers were the technological successors of the ''Venator''-class Jedi cruisers used by the [[Republic Navy|naval forces]] of the Galactic Republic during the Clone Wars. After the Republic was [[Proclamation of the New Order|turned]] into the Empire at the end of the Clone Wars, the self-anointed [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] decreed a massive military buildup. To meet interstellar defense needs, the great shipyards of the galaxy were fired up during the Clone Wars and remained lit well into the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]]. The enormous construction facilities at [[Kuat]], [[Corellia]], [[Ringo Vinda]], [[Fondor]], and elsewhere were converted from civilian graving docks into military starports capable of churning out ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers.<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> Building upon the strengths of the Jedi cruisers, the bigger ''Imperial''-class vessels became one of the most instantly recognizable symbols of the Imperial might, and were often titled intimidating names such as ''[[Lawbringer]]'', ''[[Relentless]]'', and ''[[Devastator]]''.<ref name="DB ISD" />

[[File:Lothal_under_siege.png|thumb|220px|Three ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers over Lothal]]
Initially, the new Star Destroyers were deployed to [[sector]]s and [[Star system|systems]] that had once been beyond the reach of Republic law, where they would subjugate them and crush any signs of resistance or rebellion. Imperial Star Destroyers became symbols of this new order. Citizens weary of chaos and war cheered the sight of these giant dagger-shaped warships, while [[pirate]]s and [[enslaver]]s quailed at the thought of confronting them. But a few citizens wondered if the imposition of Imperial law was worth the freedoms lost.<ref name="DB ISD" />

Easily becoming the most recognizable symbol of Imperial power, the ''Imperial''-class further demonstrated its tactical versatility by protecting galactic commerce and bolstering Imperial-backed governments. Many [[admiral]]s, [[Grand Moff]]s, [[Imperial Security Bureau|ISB]] [[agent]]s and [[Senior Commander|senior Imperial commanders]] utilized these ships as their personal command ship, with the ship's officer often being as intimidating as the ship itself—whose shadow alone could bring results.<ref name="USW NE" /> At the peak of the Empire, over 25,000 Imperial Star Destroyers were in existence<ref name="SWU">''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''</ref> with 24 assigned to each of the 1,024 [[sector|regional sectors]] to form independent [[Sector Group]]s.<ref name="SW BMF 20" /> The Empire's primary source of Star Destroyers and Destroyer-equipped shipyards was located at the industrial manufacturing center of Kuat. Ultimately, these giant craft became the backbone of the Imperial Navy, hunting down Rebel task forces, blockading undisciplined worlds and serving as launch bases for planetary assaults.<ref name="DB ISD" />

Eventually, the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer would be replaced by the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]]. The ''Devastator'' was the last of the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers to lumber out of the Kuat Drive Yards before the facility began production on the ''Imperial II''-class,<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> although it was later upgraded to compete with these more advanced warships.<ref name="BS">{{InsiderCite|issue1=149|issue2=150|Blade Squadron (short story)}}</ref>

The ''Imperial''-class would ultimately see service in the [[First Order]]'s [[First Order Navy|Navy]] thirty years after the [[Battle of Endor]], and would be regarded as a highly respected ship, with many of its design flaws rectified with the construction of the [[Resurgent-class Star Destroyer|''Resurgent''-class Star Destroyer]], a newer, more powerful vessel based on the Old Empire's dreaded warships.<ref name="Before the Awakening">''[[Before the Awakening]]''</ref> [[35 ABY|35 years after the Battle of Yavin]], the [[Sith Eternal]] used [[Xyston-class Star Destroyer|''Xyston''-class Star Destroyers]]. These Star Destroyers were based directly on the design of the ''Imperial-I''-class Star Destroyer, with the primary exception being that the ''Xyston''-class was armed with a [[Axial superlaser|planet-killing weapon]].<ref name="TROSVD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Some inconsistencies concerning the armament of the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer has been presented in several sources. The [[Fantasy Flight Games]] [[Roleplaying game|RPG]] sourcebook ''[[Starships and Speeders]]'', published in states that the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer possessed both light and heavy turbolaser batteries, and two different types of ion cannons.<ref name="Starships and Speeders" /> However, ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' does not support different ion cannons or light and heavy turbolasers,<ref name="SW ROUVG" /> and ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''<ref name="USW NE" /> and ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]''<ref name="SW DORVG" /> state that it had 60 [[Taim & Bak]] [[XX-9 heavy turbolaser battery|XX-9 heavy turbolaser batteries]] and 60 [[Borstel Galactic Defense|Borstel]] [[NK-7 ion cannon]]s.<ref name="USW NE" /> This article assumes the armament information from ''Starships and Speeders'' is incorrect. A volume of the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' series of reference booklets, ''[[Starships of the Empire and the Rebellion]]'' contains annotations over a port lateral side-view of what is denoted as an ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer that outline [[concussion missile launcher]]s present on the [[conning tower]] and fore brim region of the starship. An earlier volume of the series ''[[Naval Weapons and Equipment]]'' asserts that the Imperial I-class possessed no such weaponry, in contrast to predecessors such as the ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer, with ion cannons superseding them. Since the majority of other sources adhere to the assertion that no concussion missile launchers were equipped onto ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyers, this article assumes ''[[Starships of the Empire and the Rebellion]]'' is incorrect.
